sasha: Quick sync — we need a solid design for tiered model throttling that handles per-org and per-key quotas but also model-family differences. Some customers hit cost/latency limits when they use 70B vs 7B models. Proposing: per-org per-family soft rate + hard burst token cap + global fallback. Thoughts?
kevin: +1 to per-family. Question: do we tag requests by model family at the gateway or let routing layer infer? tagging earlier is simpler for enforcement.
maria: tagging at gateway makes sense. Also need to account for composite requests where tool calls hit different models. Counting should be token-based not request-based.
aj: Implementation thought: weight tokens by model size. e.g. weight=1 for 7B, weight=4 for 70B. Enforcement uses weighted_token_sum over sliding window. If > limit -> 429 or queue depending on policy. Pseudocode below:
```
# quota config example
quota: 
  scope: org
  family: llama-70b
  rate: 10rps
  burst_tokens: 200000
  weight: 4

# enforcement sketch
consume = incoming_tokens * model_weight
if sliding_window_sum + consume > burst_tokens: reject/queue
else increment counters and allow
```
kevin: Two quick caveats: (1) people can cheat by switching to many smaller families to get more throughput; (2) some models have higher latency — a pure rps limit could punish low-latency small models. We need cross-family global cap and maybe per-model latency SLO awareness in routing.
sasha: Good points. Proposal: tiered controls: per-family soft quota + global hard token quota per-org. Also allow tier pins: e.g., enterprise tenants can reserve family shares (dedicated capacity).
maria: UX: In Console show stacked bars per family (used vs quota), projected burn if current traffic continues, and a slider to reserve family share for a key. Also a note if a key is hitting weighted-throttle often with suggestions (lower temp, smaller model).
aj: Telemetry needs: family_token_count, family_rejects, family_queue_time, per-key-family_histogram. We should expose these in traces so SRE can correlate spikes to model rollouts.
ops-bot: deploy-bot scheduled: canary rule deployment window tomorrow 02:00-03:00 UTC for quota matcher change.
kevin: For enforcement we need an efficient matcher: avoid per-request DB lookups. Cache quota rules in the gateway with TTL and do atomic token-bucket ops in Redis (Lua) or in-memory leaky-bucket with fallback.
sasha: Action items: (1) @aj to prototype quota matcher with family tag + weighted tokens (PR), (2) @maria to mock Console family usage UI, (3) infra to add family metrics to ingestion pipeline (kevin volunteered to scope), (4) ops to run canary (deploy-bot noted).
maria: I'll mock a Console panel and post screenshots. Should include an override modal for specific API keys.
aj: Starting a spike tonight — will push WIP PR and link it here.
sasha: Thanks — let's keep it lightweight. If we can ship weighted family throttling in a controlled canary, we can reduce 70B noise without blocking small-model throughput. :thumbsup:
kevin: One more: need docs for partners about how token weighting affects billing and quotas. Otherwise support will get swamped.
sasha: Agreed — add a short FAQ and doc page to deploy with the change.
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: Canary queued for prod-1 at 2026-04-02T02:00:00Z.
maria: great, thanks everyone. I'll start mocks and post by EOD.
aj: PR up in a few hours, marking draft.
sasha: Ok closing the thread — will follow up in a few days with status.
